span: and (c) When directed by an official traffic control device.
proposal: A control-device atom for an official traffic control device that directs road users to display lighted lamps (headlamps on), on the travel regions it governs (dev.governs), with the same structured conditions attribute as dev.zone_sign (proposed: dev.lamp_use_sign). f7 is condition (c): it decides when the lamp duty applies, namely when a device directs it even though neither darkness (f5, env.darkness) nor poor visibility (f6, env.visibility) does. Without it, the rule cannot tell a stretch where a device directs lamp use from any other stretch, so it misses that part of the duty's domain. The words state no other observable fact for that limb. It is not a legal region class: the direction is a feature displayed on the road, so it cannot be an assumption. A condition span cannot be narrowed or dropped. Writing it with the atoms the record maps (some dev.regulatory_sign governing a travel region x occupies) would make the duty apply under any no-parking, one-way or truck-route sign, which is a different condition.
nearest: dev.regulatory_sign: 'a point regulation by catalogue code ... no_left_turn, no_right_turn, no_u_turn, no_straight, one_way, keep_right, do_not_enter, wrong_way, no_stopping, no_standing, no_parking, angle_parking, right_turn_only, entrance, exit, closed_to_traffic, exempt_crossing, abandoned_crossing, shoulder_use_permitted, bicycles_prohibited, pedestrians_prohibited, nonmotorized_prohibited, motor_vehicles_prohibited, truck_route, no_trucks' — no code is a direction to display lamps, and a code not listed is an ontology change request

dev.zone_sign: 'kind ∈ {school, school_crossing, pedestrian_safety, temporary_traffic_control, no_passing, high_occupancy_lane, heavy_vehicle_lane, speed_zone, narrow_highway, hazardous_place, parking_restricted, trail}' — no kind is a lamp-use zone
dev.governs: 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls' — it locates what a device controls; it says nothing about what the device directs
env.darkness / env.visibility: these carry limbs (a) and (b), the light conditions, not a device's direction, and limb (c) applies regardless of either
